reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about dislocation behavior, lattice distortion effects, and strengthening mechanisms in refractory BCC HEAs, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the proposed edge-dislocation dominance in these specific alloys, so the lack of cited support leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: Severe lattice distortion in refractory BCC HEAs promotes edge dislocation-mediated plasticity over screw dislocation flow
Edge dislocations have lower intrinsic mobility than screw dislocations in this environment
Edge dislocation pinning is the primary driver of elevated hardness and high-temperature strength
Reducing lattice distortion will restore conventional screw-dislocation-dominated flow and lower strength
The fraction and mobility of edge vs. screw dislocations can be quantified by in situ TEM and neutron diffraction
